title: Sherwood mnemonic proof words with shared types, conversions and figure context
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. An owned19-mode medieval mnemonic gives reusable proposition-type and proof-operation cues within words. Full fapesmo/campestres reductions constrain shared arguments; campestres, b+r and the third-figure source conflict remain uncorrected. No target writer is claimed.

design.access: Existing external source cache plus one official public historical edition; all cited source pages viewed natively. No new Voynich source/image, reserved material, target fit, root Trotula files or GDT987 runtime/result reads.

source_evidence.quote: ## B. Sherwood: mnemonic words combine proposition types and proof operations

source.author: William of Sherwood
source.ownership: Complete19-mode mnemonic and corresponding prose classification; conversion and figure prerequisites; two complete worked reductions; all source conflicts retained. The underlying BnF witness and second edition have not been collated.

design.new_consequence: Shared type and transformation cues within a mnemonic must preserve three class identities through premise conversion, exchange and conclusion. The same AII types cease to entail their conclusion if the figure changes.

figure_roles.1: middle is subject of major and predicate of minor for direct moods
figure_roles.2: middle is predicate in both premises
figure_roles.3: middle is subject in both premises

source_operations.s: per-se conversion: reverse arguments and preserve quality/quantity; source explicitly licenses E and I
source_operations.p: per-accidens conversion: A(X,Y) to I(Y,X), conditional on nonempty X in modern semantics
source_operations.b_and_r: Printed same-word condition for reductio; nonselective and not silently changed to b+c

finite_productions: Proof := Figure + three shared class-references + Mode + certified reduction
finite_semantic_inventory.prohibited: No free consonant fillers, per-word clue dictionaries, invisible premises or locally renamed class identities.

owned_fapesmo.condition: H nonempty for the modern set-theoretic expansion. The source prints no separate existential premise.
owned_fapesmo.printed_major_reading: quod animal est homo; quod is not silently changed to quoddam

owned_campestres.conflict: Printed p in campestres is not represented by a per-accidens operation in the described reduction.

genuine_rival.meaning: Figure2 premises true and conclusion false; a type-only classifier with free incidence cannot distinguish this.

source_uncertainties: First-three-vowel and preceding-vowel attachment are inferred crosswalks to the prose, not stated universal clauses in the bounded mnemonic explanation.
campestres is preserved with p; no modernization to Camestres.
Printed b+r rule also includes Barbara and baralipton, so it does not uniquely select baroco and bocardo.
Printed final third-figure major-negative prohibition conflicts with the preceding negative-major worked modes; maiori is preserved.
An actual fixed test needs a source-faithful bounded subset or witness collation before fitting, without suppressing disagreements.
symmetries: A simultaneous permutation of all class names preserves logical validity; this alone cannot recover human, stone, animal or pearl.
Figure context and class references are not encoded by a mnemonic alone.
